turns.learner: Hello! Can you give me an exercise on he, she and it with -s?
turns.tutor: Hello! Certainly. In the present simple, third person singular verbs take -s, or -es after -sh, -ch, -s, -x and -o, and consonant + y becomes -ies. Let's start with a spelling one: She ___ (watch) TV after dinner. Answer with only the verb.

W1 (wrong) strength 0: the verb does not change after he/she/it. Its error: leaves the verb unchanged after he/she/it ("She like tea").
W2 (wrong) strength 0: -s goes on every verb and -es/-ies are not needed. Its error: adds -s wrongly or misspells -es/-ies ("She watchs TV", "I plays").
C1 (correct) strength 3: add -s/-es after he/she/it. Independent correct productions so far: 0.
C2 (correct) strength 3: -es after sh/ch/s/x/o, -ies after consonant + y, no -s after I/you/we/they. Independent correct productions so far: 0.
